summary: Explains that role handlers go into the play's global handler scope, so they can be used outside the role and can clash with same-named handlers. Notify `role_name : handler_name` to target the role's handler; handlers notified in `roles` are flushed at the end of `tasks`.
questions: Can I notify a handler defined in a role from my playbook tasks?
How do I make sure the role's handler is called and not one with the same name elsewhere?
When do handlers notified by roles run?

answer_card.title: Handlers in roles
answer_card.answer_md:
Role handlers are inserted into the play's global handler scope, so they can be notified from outside the role, and their names can collide with other handlers. To target a role's handler specifically, notify it as:

```yaml
notify: "role_name : handler_name"
```
Handlers notified within the `roles` section are automatically flushed at the end of the `tasks` section.
